title: Tycho-2-to-Gaia proper motions of 58 detached binaries reject dark third bodies as the cause of all ASAS-3-to-TESS period changes; luminous third bodies near the pair-star mass remain possible
abstract: Campaign study 02d77ae9 found common-mode period changes between ASAS-3 (2000-2009) and TESS (2018-2026) eclipse times in 77 of 304 detached southern binaries and interpreted them as light-travel-time effects (LTTE) of third stars with orbits of decades. An LTTE third body must also move the binary on the sky. We measured the proper-motion anomaly of each binary: the Gaia DR3 proper motion minus the long-term proper motion from the Tycho-2 mean position (mean epoch 1954-1992) to the Gaia DR3 position. 53,884 field stars of the same brightness calibrate the errors (scale 1.10, 3.3 percent outliers). For each common-mode binary we drew third-body orbits from the 02d77ae9 prior, weighted them by their fit to all TESS and ASAS-3 eclipse times, and predicted the anomaly for dark and for main-sequence third bodies. 58 common-mode binaries have usable astrometry. They have a small excess over 185 binaries without a period change and over field stars (r^2 > 9.21 in 8.6, 5.4 and 5.4 percent), and four binaries show clear anomalies that agree with LTTE (for example ASAS 062428+1217.2, r^2 = 31). But a mixture model gives an LTTE fraction f = 0.27 (90 percent 0.07-0.53) for dark third bodies; f = 1 is worse by 13.1 in log-likelihood and no simulation with f = 1 gives a value this low. For main-sequence third bodies f = 0.39 (0.10-0.77; 1 of 200 simulations with f = 1 is this low). f = 1 is possible only if the third bodies have about the mass of one eclipsing star (m3/M12 = 0.35-0.65), where the light centre almost does not move, or with a light limit from the eclipse depths (f = 0.55, 0.13-0.93). Fits that use only the link-test numbers, a Gaussian noise model and quality subsets give the same result. Limits: Tycho-2 errors (about 1.2 mas/yr) restrict the test to binaries within about 1 kpc; the predictions depend on the third-body prior and on a twin-pair L ~ M^4 light model; no spectroscopy was used.

Harvard plate test of the same period changes; our independent astrometry agrees that LTTE does not explain all changes and disfavours dark third bodies as a population-wide explanation.
